// 32 bytes\n  manifestHash: Uint8Array; // 4 bytes - CRC-32 of manifest (roots beacon->manifest->blocks chain)\n  filename: string;\n  mimeType: string;\n}\n\n/**\n * Validation error with code and details.\n */\nexport class BeaconValidationError extends Error {\n  constructor(\n    public code: string,\n    message: string,\n    public details: Record<string, unknown>\n  ) {\n    super(message);\n    this.name = 'BeaconValidationError';\n  }\n}\n\n/**\n * Maximum safe values for beacon fields (T1).\n *\n * **Beacon size bound calculation (R1's 256-byte payload):**\n * - Fixed fields: 64 bytes (streamId, wireVersion, originalSize, payloadLen, blockSize,\n *                  blockCount, fragmentLen, degreeCap, flags, blockHashLen,\n *                  wholeFileHash, manifestHash)\n * - CRC-32: 4 bytes\n * - Length prefixes: 2 bytes (1 byte each for filename and mimeType)\n * - Available for filename + mimeType: 256 - 64 - 4 - 2 = 186 bytes\n *\n * This yields a conservative allocation of 128 bytes for filename and 58 bytes for\n * mimeType, ensuring the beacon never overflows R1's capacity while accommodating\n * common filenames and MIME types.\n */\nexport const BEACON_LIMITS = {\n  MAX_L: 4096,\n  MAX_BLOCK_COUNT: 16_700_000, // 16.7M blocks × 192 KB = 3.0 TB\n  MAX_FILE_SIZE: 281_474_976_710_656, // 281 TB, 6-byte field max\n  /** Maximum number of blocks that the manifest itself can consume (T1). */\n  /** K_manifest = ceil(blockCount × blockHashLen / BLOCK). Limits DoS from unbounded manifest growth. */\n  MAX_K_MANIFEST_BLOCKS: 1000, // 1000 manifest blocks ≈ 195 MB of manifest data\n  /** Maximum UTF-8 encoded filename length in bytes (T2). Chosen to fit within R1's 256-byte payload. */\n  MAX_FILENAME_BYTES: 128,\n  /** Maximum UTF-8 encoded MIME type length in bytes (T2). Chosen to fit within R1's 256-byte payload. */\n  MAX_MIMETYPE_BYTES: 58,\n  /** Maximum UTF-8 codepoint count for filename (T2). A UTF-8 string can use up to 4 bytes per codepoint. */\n  MAX_FILENAME_CODEPOINTS: 32, // 32 × 4 = 128, guarantees never exceeds MAX_FILENAME_BYTES\n  /** Maximum UTF-8 codepoint count for MIME type (T2). */\n  MAX_MIMETYPE_CODEPOINTS: 14, // 14 × 4 = 56, fits within MAX_MIMETYPE_BYTES\n} as const;\n\n/**\n * Calculate K_manifest from blockCount and blockHashLen.\n *\n * K_manifest is the number of blocks needed to store the block hash manifest.\n * The manifest contains blockCount × blockHashLen bytes (all block hashes),\n * divided into blocks of size BLOCK (196608 bytes = K × L).\n *\n * Formula: K_manifest = ceil(blockCount × blockHashLen / BLOCK)\n *\n * @param blockCount - Number of data blocks (from beacon)\n * @param blockHashLen - Length of each block hash in bytes (from beacon)\n * @returns Number of blocks needed to store the manifest\n */\nfunction calculateKManifest(blockCount: number, blockHashLen: number): number {\n  const BLOCK = 196608; // K × L where K=768, L=256 (from core/params.ts)\n  const manifestBytes = blockCount * blockHashLen;\n  return Math.ceil(manifestBytes / BLOCK);\n}\n\n/**\n * Device context for K validation logging.\n */\nexport interface DeviceContext {\n  /** Device signature from GE benchmark cache */\n  deviceSignature: string;\n  /** User agent string */\n  userAgent: string;\n  /** Platform identifier */\n  platform: string;\n}\n\n/**\n * Parse a beacon from bytes.\n *\n * Beacon format: [body fields...][crc32(4)]\n * The CRC-32 covers all beacon body fields and MUST be validated before\n * any metadata (including streamId) is trusted.\n *\n * **Validation order is critical:**\n * 1. @throws {BeaconValidationError} If any field fails validation or CRC-32 mismatch\n */\nexport function parseBeacon(\n  bytes: Uint8Array,\n  localKMax: number,\n  availableQuota: number,\n  deviceContext?: DeviceContext\n): BeaconMeta {\n  let offset = 0;\n\n  const readU32 = (): number => {\n    const value = (bytes[offset]! << 24) |\n                 (bytes[offset + 1]! << 16) |\n                 (bytes[offset + 2]! << 8) |\n                 bytes[offset + 3]!;\n    offset += 4;\n    return value >>> 0; // Force unsigned\n  };\n\n  const readU24 = (): number => {\n    const value = (bytes[offset]! << 16) |\n                 (bytes[offset + 1]! << 8) |\n                 bytes[offset + 2]!;\n    offset += 3;\n    return value >>> 0;\n  };\n\n  const readU16 = (): number => {\n    const value = (bytes[offset]! << 8) | bytes[offset + 1]!;\n    offset += 2;\n    return value >>> 0;\n  };\n\n  const readU8 = (): number => {\n    const value = bytes[offset]!;\n    offset += 1;\n    return value;\n  };\n\n  const readBytes = (n: number): Uint8Array => {\n    const value = bytes.subarray(offset, offset + n);\n    offset += n;\n    return value;\n  };\n\n  const readString = (maxLen: number) => {\n    const len = readU8();\n    if (len > maxLen) {\n      throw new BeaconValidationError(\n        'E-META-BOUNDS',\n        `String length ${len} exceeds maximum ${maxLen}`,\n expected ${expectedSize} (body+CRC)`,\n      {actual: bytes.length, expected: expectedSize}\n    );\n  }\n\n  // Read the CRC-32 from the last 4 bytes\n  const storedCrc = ((bytes[offset]! << 24) |\n                    (bytes[offset + 1]! << 16) |\n                    (bytes[offset + 2]! << 8) |\n                    bytes[offset + 3]!) >>> 0; // Force unsigned\n\n  // Calculate CRC-32 over the beacon body (everything except the last 4 bytes)\n  const calculatedCrc = crc32(bytes.subarray(0, beaconBodySize));\n\n  if (storedCrc !== calculatedCrc) {\n    throw new BeaconValidationError(\n      'E-CRC-MISMATCH',\n      `Beacon CRC-32 mismatch: stored=${storedCrc} calculated=${calculatedCrc}`,\n      {stored: storedCrc, calculated: calculatedCrc}\n    );\n  }\n\n  // blockHashLen);\n  if (blockCountManifest > BEACON_LIMITS.MAX_K_MANIFEST_BLOCKS) {\n    throw new BeaconValidationError(\n      'E-META-BOUNDS',\n      `Manifest block count (${blockCountManifest}) Objective\n32\t\n33\t> **A static website that accepts a file from the user and turns it into a visual\n34\t> transmission on screen, which a second device running the same page receives through\n35\t> its camera and reconstructs into the original file.**\n36\t>\n37\t> **It must handle large files — on the order of multiple gigabytes.**\n38\t\n39\t- **Static.** No backend. The\n48\tdesign must never *forbid* a large file, run out of memory, or blow up super-linearly.\n49\tBut the channel's physics are what they are:\n50\t\n51\t| File size | Stage 1 (30 KB/s) | Stage 2 (60 KB/s) | Stage 3 (106 KB/s) |\n52\t|---|---|---|---|\n53\t| 100 MB | 57 min | 28 min | 16 min |\n54\t| **1 GB** | **9.7 h** | **4.9 h** | **2.7 h** |\n55\t| **10 GB** | **4.0 days** | **2.0 days** | **27.5 h** |\n56\t| 100 GB | 40.5 days | 20.2 days | 11.4 days |\n57\t| 1 TB | 414 days | 207 days | 117 days |\n58\t\n59\t> All figures are **user-visible file bytes**, not wire bytes. See §13.2 — with\n60\t> compression on, the two differ by 3–10× on compressible input, and quoting the wrong\n61\t> one would overstate throughput.\n62\t\n63\t**Gigabytes are hours-to-days. Terabytes are months.** Three design consequences follow,\n64\tand they are as load-bearing as any coding decision:\n65\t\n66\t1. **Resume is not optional** (D22). Nobody holds a phone for 27 hours.\n67\t2. **Neither side may hold the file in memory** (D20).\n68\t3. **The app states the estimated time before the user commits** (D23). Letting someone\n69\t   start a 40-day transfer without saying so is a product failure, not an edge case.\n70\t\n71\t---\n72\t\n73\t## 2. Glossary\n74\t\n75\tSeveral of these words are overloaded in the surrounding literature, and two of them\n76\t(*block*, *frame*) mean different things in different research documents. Within this\n77\tplan they mean exactly this:\n78\t\n79\t| Term | Meaning here |\n80\t|---|---|\n81\t| **Fragment** | The atomic unit the fountain code operates over. Fixed length **L** for the whole session (D15). |\n82\t| **K** | Number of fragments in one block. Derived as `blockSize / L`; never transmitted (D7). |\n83\t| **Block** | A contiguous slice of the (possibly compressed) payload, cut into K fragments and fountain-coded independently. **Always means this** — never \"fountain block\" or \"QR block\". |\n84\t| **Packet** | One fountain-coded symbol: 13-byte header + L payload bytes. The unit a tile carries. |\n85\t| **Tile** | One QR symbol on screen. Carries exactly one packet. |\n86\t| **Frame** | One displayed image, containing a grid of tiles. **Never** a video frame — those are *camera frames*. |\n87\t| **Camera frame** | One image captured by the receiver's camera. |\n88\t| **Beacon** | A special **packet** carrying file-level metadata instead of payload. Beacon packets are encoded into tiles and mixed into display frames by the frame mixer (D17, §7.2). |\n89\t| **Profile** | A modulation configuration: QR version, module pixel size, tile count. Several coexist per frame (D16). |\n90\t| **Dwell** | How many packets the sender emits for one block before advancing (§8.1). |\n91\t| **Screen px** | A pixel on the *sender's display*. What the renderer controls. |\n92\t| **Camera px** | A pixel in the *receiver's captured frame*. What the decoder actually sees. |\n93\t| **px/module** | **Always CAMERA px per module unless explicitly written \"screen px/module\".** The 4 px/module decode cliff is a *camera*-pixel figure. Conflating the two put every S2/S3 optical run below the cliff — see `../notes/spike-results.md` §S3. |\n94\t| **Magnification** | `camera_px_per_module = screen_px_per_module × M`, where `M` = (capture width across the code region) / (code region width in screen px). A 1920-px-wide landscape code region filling a 1080-px-wide portrait capture gives **M = 0.5625**, so 4 screen px/module is only **2.25 camera px/module**. |\n95\t| **Erasure** | A packet that did not arrive or failed validation. Never a corrupted packet — those are discarded, not used. |\n96\t| **Stage** | A modulation generation: 1 = tiled mono QR, 2 = + RGB tripling, 3 = custom grid codec. |\n97\t| **Pass** | One complete traversal of every block by the sender. |\n98\t\n99\t---"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"550ae08e-93e1-4006-af9f-f7de19392fad","uuid":"68bcaf19-a1fb-4bb8-8239-ead4bddd53a0","timestamp":"2026-08-02T20:41:35.472Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/home/coding/screenferry/docs/plan/plan.md","content":"# screenferry — Application Plan\n\nSingle source of truth for what screenferry is, how it is built, and in what order.\nConstraints it must satisfy live in [`../notes/concept.md`](../notes/concept.md); the\nevidence behind every number lives in [`../research/`](../research/).\n\n**Status:** research complete (9 threads). **Phase 0 partial, Phase 0.5 partial, Phase 1 built**\n(22 tests green) — see §17 for exactly what is and is not done. Objective\n\n> **A static website that accepts a file from the user and turns it into a visual\n> transmission on screen, which a second device running the same page receives through\n> its camera and reconstructs into the original file.**\n>\n> **It must handle large files — on the order of multiple gigabytes.**\n\n- **Static.** No backend. Files on a CDN, works offline, auditable once and trusted\n  thereafter. There is nowhere to upload anything *to*.\n- **Same page, both roles.** One deployment; the user picks sender or receiver.\n- **Screen → camera is the only channel.** Strictly one-way, lossy, low-bandwidth.\n- **Multi-gigabyte.** The requirement that most shapes the architecture (§3).\n\n### 1.1 The honest framing of \"multiple gigabytes\"\n\nMulti-GB support is an **architectural** requirement, not a performance promise. The\ndesign must never *forbid* a large file, run out of memory, or blow up super-linearly.\nBut the channel's physics are what they are:\n\n| File size | Stage 1 (30 KB/s) | Stage 2 (60 KB/s) | Stage 3 (106 KB/s) |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 100 MB | 57 min | 28 min | 16 min |\n| **1 GB** | **9.7 h** | **4.9 h** | **2.7 h** |\n| **10 GB** | **4.0 days** | **2.0 days** | **27.5 h** |\n| 100 GB | 40.5 days | 20.2 days | 11.4 days |\n| 1 TB | 414 days | 207 days | 117 days |\n\n> All figures are **user-visible file bytes**, not wire bytes. See §13.2 — with\n> compression on, the two differ by 3–10× on compressible input, and quoting the wrong\n> one would overstate throughput.\n\n**Gigabytes are hours-to-days. Terabytes are months.** Three design consequences follow,\nand they are as load-bearing as any coding decision:\n\n1. **Resume is not optional** (D22). Nobody holds a phone for 27 hours.\n2. **Neither side may hold the file in memory** (D20).\n3. **The app states the estimated time before the user commits** (D23). Letting someone\n   start a 40-day transfer without saying so is a product failure, not an edge case.\n\n---\n\n## 2. Glossary\n\nSeveral of these words are overloaded in the surrounding literature, and two of them\n(*block*, *frame*) mean different things in different research documents. Within this\nplan they mean exactly this:\n\n| Term | Meaning here |\n|---|---|\n| **Fragment** | The atomic unit the fountain code operates over. Fixed length **L** for the whole session (D15). |\n| **K** | Number of fragments in one block. Derived as `blockSize / L`; never transmitted (D7). |\n| **Block** | A contiguous slice of the (possibly compressed) payload, cut into K fragments and fountain-coded independently. **Always means this** — never \"fountain block\" or \"QR block\". |\n| **Packet** | One fountain-coded symbol: 13-byte header + L payload bytes. The unit a tile carries. |\n| **Tile** | One QR symbol on screen. Carries exactly one packet. |\n| **Frame** | One displayed image, containing a grid of tiles. **Never** a video frame — those are *camera frames*. |\n| **Camera frame** | One image captured by the receiver's camera. |\n| **Beacon** | A special **packet** carrying file-level metadata instead of payload. Beacon packets are encoded into tiles and mixed into display frames by the frame mixer (D17, §7.2). |\n| **Profile** | A modulation configuration: QR version, module pixel size, tile count. Several coexist per frame (D16). |\n| **Dwell** | How many packets the sender emits for one block before advancing (§8.1). |\n| **Screen px** | A pixel on the *sender's display*. What the renderer controls. |\n| **Camera px** | A pixel in the *receiver's captured frame*. What the decoder actually sees. |\n| **px/module** | **Always CAMERA px per module unless explicitly written \"screen px/module\".** The 4 px/module decode cliff is a *camera*-pixel figure. Conflating the two put every S2/S3 optical run below the cliff — see `../notes/spike-results.md` §S3. |\n| **Magnification** | `camera_px_per_module = screen_px_per_module × M`, where `M` = (capture width across the code region) / (code region width in screen px). A 1920-px-wide landscape code region filling a 1080-px-wide portrait capture gives **M = 0.5625**, so 4 screen px/module is only **2.25 camera px/module**. |\n| **Erasure** | A packet that did not arrive or failed validation. Never a corrupted packet — those are discarded, not used. |\n| **Stage** | A modulation generation: 1 = tiled mono QR, 2 = + RGB tripling, 3 = custom grid codec. |\n| **Pass** | One complete traversal of every block by the sender. |\n\n---","numLines":100,"startLine":0,"totalLines":1540}}}
